name: crypto-aesgcm256-short
algorithm: std AES-256-GCM (NIST SP 800-38D, 96-bit nonce) seal then open of every 64-byte record of splitmix64 bytes, one key object for the run, a fresh nonce per record, a 13-byte aad, reps passes (mk/crypto-aesgcm256-short.mk): the cost per call.

skip.c: no std crypto: C has no standard AEAD
skip.rust: no std crypto: Rust std has no AEAD; the aes-gcm crate is third-party, and no crate stands in (plan/06-m6.md 4.1)

notes: Work per step: one seal and one open of one 64-byte record with a 13-byte aad (four blocks of text, one of aad, the length block and the tag's block per call), so the row measures what a call costs beside its blocks: the counter setup, the GHASH key's use and the tag. Mk AesGcm.New once; Go cipher.NewGCM once; Zig aead.aes_gcm.Aes256Gcm.encrypt and decrypt, which expand the key on every call (Zig's std has no key object), a cost that dominates at this size and is labelled here. Records per second = mib * 16384 * reps / median.
Instruction paths as in crypto-aesgcm128's notes.

Checksums from the go column (GOAMD64=v2 -pgo=off, Go 1.27, owner's machine, 2026-11-12); the Mk column (mk build --release, mk from the tree) printed the same at both arg sets. Written by the std-crypto2 lane. Not published: no number here is a measurement.
